cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Take the Consequence
cards.instruction: Get them to accept responsibility for carrying out the cost, penalty, or unpleasant next step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've cancelled the outing, following your cross on the booking form. You'll need to tell the team.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That cross selected the coach company. You copied it into the cancellation box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, the booking decision. You can explain it; you chose the company.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ring them to restore it, but you tell the team about the mistake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Make that call with the team here. Then you can explain the cancellation to everyone at once.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 follows B's cross as cancellation; B2 identifies selection versus cancellation fields. A3 covers and A5 shifts the unpleasant announcement into B's repair call.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 exact form error causes A3 chosen-company justification; B4 restoration offer gives A5 the call to make public.

relationship.evidence: B4 offers a genuine fix while asking A to own the mistake; B is neither passive nor a question feeder.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts B4 helpful phone call into the unpleasant public explanation A wants B to perform.

specificity.evidence: A1 cancellation and B2 form fields now establish what happened without an invented budget mechanism.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 make the call with the team here is an actionable tactical change, with a clear audience reason.
